items.title: Dick Hyman interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clearwater Beach, Florida, March 17, 2001 [interview 2 of 2]
items.q: And one time Mitch Miller needed something or other which involved slapping your hands on your thighs like [slaps] and don’t you know I volunteered to do that.

ctx.x: That’s great. I love hearing that stuff. I mean you did, you know people think of you as someone who can do anything.

I’ve done my best. I know it’s not true. I know quite a few things I can’t do. But I was willing to try almost anything. Another time, well I was, well I look at it now that I’ve become a kind of elder curmudgeon, when I look back at it I was amazingly cooperative and supportive in those days. And if the percussion section seemed to be short one effect or another I would jump in and play claves or maracas or other Latin sort of things. And one time Mitch Miller needed something or other which involved slapping…
I don’t suppose you could hit up AFTRA for workman’s comp.
